candidate.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting: Why It Works
candidate.description:
Why do AIs miss easy questions—and how can a single sentence fix it?

This video explains Chain-of-Thought prompting (CoT)—the idea of asking models to show their work step by step. With a simple “apples” word problem and real benchmarks, you’ll see how CoT turns shortcut guesses into explicit reasoning and why the gains become dramatic at large model scales. On the GSM8K math benchmark, for example, PaLM 540B rises from about 18% with a standard prompt to about 57% with chain-of-thought, illustrating an emergent ability unlocked by model size. You can apply this today in any mainstream LLM: add a short instruction like “Let’s think step by step” or “Show your work,” and when possible include a compact example in the question → reasoning → answer format. CoT not only improves performance on multi-step tasks (math word problems, planning, rule following) but also makes the model’s logic auditable so you can verify each step—not just the final answer.
